productContexts.label: Figure 1 transferred Ag nanocrystal wire film on PMMA
notes: The article explicitly ties Figure 1 to the Ag nanocrystal film transferred at 15–20 mN/m.
The ~3 µL stock drop is reported for most experiments, not specifically proven for this micrograph.
Study-wide 20–300 nm wire-width control and 1–2 µm wire lengths are not assigned as exact Figure 1 specimen measurements.

The article later amplifies the Ag wire mask and uses it to pattern PMMA/silicon; those downstream device outputs are not new Ag nanocrystal synthesis records. The article does not identify whether the Figure 1 transferred film was imaged before or after mask amplification. The stable 'monolayer' record and sample identifiers do not establish a measured layer count for Figure 1.

intuition.title: What this step controls
intuition.text: The reported trough temperature and transfer surface pressure describe formation and collection of Ag nanocrystal wires; no sample-specific wire width or core crystal phase is assigned.

general_background.title: Thermodynamics and kinetics
general_background.summary: Thermodynamics describes which states are energetically favoured, while kinetics governs how quickly a system can move between them. A change can be favourable yet proceed slowly when an activation barrier or limited transport restricts the pathway.
